items.followUp: State the relation between the net force on an object and its rate of change of momentum.

rubric.why: States how force is related to momentum.
rubric.description: Force is the rate of change of momentum.
rubric.how: Award for the correct verbal relation or formula.

rubric.why: Completes the vector relation between force and momentum.
rubric.description: The force acts in the direction of the change in momentum.
rubric.how: Award for stating the direction relationship.

modelAnswer: Force is the rate of change of momentum.
F = change in momentum ÷ time interval, or F = Δp/Δt.
The force acts in the direction of the change in momentum.

items.followUp: A force changes an object's momentum by 12 kg m s⁻¹. If the normal reaction is 30 N, calculate the coefficient of friction when this is the limiting friction.

rubric.why: Gives the defining ratio for coefficient of friction.
rubric.description: Coefficient of friction is the ratio of limiting friction to normal reaction.
rubric.how: Award for the correct ratio, stated in words or as a fraction.

rubric.why: Identifies the standard symbol/form and its nature.
rubric.description: It is represented by μ and has no unit.
rubric.how: Award for the symbol with the ratio or for stating that the coefficient is dimensionless.

modelAnswer: The coefficient of friction is the ratio of limiting friction to the normal reaction.
μ = limiting friction ÷ normal reaction.
It has no unit.

items.followUp: Define gravitational field strength and state its approximate value at the surface of the Moon.

rubric.why: Gives the definition of gravitational field strength.
rubric.description: Gravitational field strength is the gravitational force acting per unit mass at a point.

rubric.why: Gives the approximate value at Earth's surface with a suitable unit.
rubric.description: Its value on Earth is approximately 9.8 N kg⁻¹ (about 10 N kg⁻¹).
rubric.how: Accept 9.8 or 10 with N/kg or m/s².

modelAnswer: Gravitational field strength is the gravitational force acting per unit mass at a point.
On Earth, its value is approximately 9.8 N kg⁻¹ (about 10 N kg⁻¹).

items.followUp: Why is the electrostatic force between two charged objects also described as a non-contact force?

rubric.description: Gravitational force acts without the objects being in physical contact.
rubric.how: Award for explicitly stating that physical contact is not needed.

rubric.why: Explains how gravitational force acts between separated bodies.
rubric.description: It acts across a distance through a gravitational field.
rubric.how: Award for referring to action at a distance or through a gravitational field.

modelAnswer: Gravitational force acts between bodies without physical contact.
It acts at a distance through the gravitational field surrounding a body.

items.followUp: What information can be obtained from a distance-time graph?

rubric.why: Gives the meaning of a graph.
rubric.description: A graph is a pictorial or graphical representation of the relationship between quantities.
rubric.how: Award for identifying a graph as a graphical representation.

rubric.description: Graphs show how quantities are related and help determine or compare their values.
rubric.how: Award for a valid use such as showing a relationship, comparing quantities, or finding values.

modelAnswer: A graph is a pictorial representation of the relationship between two quantities.
It is used to show how quantities are related and to find or compare their values.

items.followUp: A block has a mass of 2 kg and a volume of 0.004 m³. Calculate its density.

rubric.why: Identifies the mass and converts the given volume to SI units.
rubric.description: Mass is 5 kg and volume is 5 L = 0.005 m³.
rubric.how: Award for correct SI data, including the litre-to-cubic-metre conversion.

rubric.why: Uses the density formula and obtains the correct result.
rubric.how: Award for the correct formula and answer with a suitable unit.

modelAnswer: Given: mass, m = 5 kg; volume, V = 5 L = 5 × 10⁻³ m³.
Formula: density, ρ = m/V.
Substitution: ρ = 5 kg ÷ 0.005 m³.
Answer: ρ = 1000 kg m⁻³.

items.followUp: Name an instrument used to measure the density of a liquid and state one liquid whose density can be checked with it.

rubric.description: A hydrometer is an instrument used to measure the density of liquids.

rubric.why: States what the instrument measures or its use.
rubric.description: It is used to measure or compare the density (or relative density) of liquids.
rubric.how: Award for a correct measurement use.

modelAnswer: A hydrometer is an instrument used to measure the density of liquids.
It is used to measure or compare the density (relative density) of different liquids.

items.followUp: Resolve a force of 20 N acting at 30° to the horizontal into horizontal and vertical components.

rubric.description: Resolution of a force is the process of splitting it into components in specified directions.
rubric.how: Award for describing the splitting of a force into components.

rubric.why: States how the components relate to the original force.
rubric.description: The vector sum of the components is equal to the original force.
rubric.how: Award for stating that the components combine vectorially to give the original force.

modelAnswer: Resolution of a force is the process of splitting a force into components in specified directions.
The vector sum of these components is equal to the original force.
